Let me analyze this OIML certificate carefully.

Certificate details:
- Number: R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.01 Rev. 1.
- Scheme: A
- Member State: Switzerland
- Issuing authority: Federal Institute of Metrology METAS, Conformity Evaluation Body METAS-Cert
- Address: Lindenweg 50, 3003 Bern-Wabern, Switzerland
- Person responsible: Gulian Couvreur, Head of METAS-Cert
- Phone: +41 58 387 01 11
- Website: www.metas.ch
- Applicant: Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co KG, Otto-Brenner-Strasse 20, 37079 Göttingen, Germany
- Manufacturer: same as applicant
- Certified type: Precision and analysis balances BC-E and BC-A Line
- Module designation: BC-EA to BC-EH, BC-AA to BC-AH
- Recommendation: OIML R 76-1, edition 2006
- Accuracy classes: (Ⅰ), (Ⅱ)
- Date issued: 21 September 2020 (3003 Bern-Wabern, 21 September 2020)
- OIML Issuing Authority: CH1

The certificate covers a family of balance models:
- BC-EA / BC-AA: Class I, Max 50 g - 320 g, e 1 mg - 2 mg, d 0.1 mg - 2 mg, n ≤ 320 000, temp range 1: +17/+27, temp range 2¹⁾: +10/+30, nominal capacity 384 g, initial zero setting + dead load²⁾ ≤ 234 g, pan size Ø 90 mm
- BC-EB / BC-AB: Class I, Max 50 g - 220 g, e 1 mg - 2 mg, d 0.1 mg - 2 mg, n ≤ 220 000, temp 1: +17/+27, temp 2¹⁾: +10/+30, nominal capacity 264 g, initial zero ≤ 214 g, pan Ø 90 mm
- BC-EB / BC-AB (again, but Class II): Max 0,1 g - 100 g, e 1 mg - 2 mg, d 0.1 mg - 2 mg, n ≤ 100 000, temp 1: +10/+30, temp 2: +10/+30, nominal 264 g, initial zero ≤ 263 g, pan Ø 90 mm

Wait, the first table has three columns but only two type names: "BC-EA BC-AA", "BC-EB BC-AB", "BC-EB BC-AB". The third column repeats BC-EB BC-AB but with Class II. That looks like an OCR issue — probably the third column should be a different type, maybe BC-EB/BC-AB has both class I and II variants? Actually, looking at typical Sartorius BC line balances: BC-EA, BC-EB, BC-EC, BC-ED, BC-EE, BC-EF, BC-EG, BC-EH. Hmm, actually the real certificate likely has BC-EA/BC-AA, BC-EB/BC-AB, and BC-EB/BC-AB repeated is suspicious. Perhaps it's actually "BC-EB BC-AB" class I and "BC-EB BC-AB" class II — some balances can be class I and class II. But Max differs: 50-220 g vs 0.1-100 g. Hmm, that seems odd for the same model.

Actually, for the purposes of extraction, I should not fabricate. I'll treat the third column as a separate variant of BC-EB/BC-AB with Class II. But model IDs should be unique... I could label them "BC-EB/BC-AB (class Ⅰ)" and "BC-EB/BC-AB (class Ⅱ)".

Wait, let me reconsider. Maybe the actual type is different, e.g., "BC-EB BC-AB" vs "BC-EB BC-AB" — OCR might have misread "BC-EC BC-AC" as "BC-EB BC-AB". But BC-EC/BC-AC appears in the second table. Hmm. Actually in the real certificate, the types might be: BC-EA/BC-AA, BC-EB/BC-AB (class I), and BC-EB/BC-AB (class II)... Actually, looking at Sartorius Cubis balances... BC line? The BC-E and BC-A line — "precision and analysis balances". Hmm.

Actually, real Sartorius balances: Entris II BCE, Practum BCA? BCE = Entris II. BCA = Practum. So BC-E = Entris II, BC-A = ? Actually "A" could be another line. The models BCE and BCA. Model designations like BCE124i, BCA124I etc. But the cert says "BC-EA to BC-EH, BC-AA to BC-AH" — so models BC-EA, BC-EB, BC-EC, BC-ED, BC-EE, BC-EF, BC-EG, BC-EH and BC-AA ... BC-AH. That's 16 models total (8 E variants + 8 A variants).

Given the tables pair them (BC-EA/BC-AA etc.), each column is a pair. So there are 8 columns total across 4 tables:

Table 1:
- Col 1: BC-EA/BC-AA, Class I, Max 50-320 g, e 1-2 mg, d 0.1-2 mg, n ≤ 320000, temp1 +17/+27, temp2¹⁾ +10/+30, nominal cap 384 g, initial zero+dead load²⁾ ≤234 g, pan Ø 90 mm
- Col 2: BC-EB/BC-AB, Class I, Max 50-220 g, e 1-2 mg, d 0.1-2 mg, n ≤ 220000, temp1 +17/+27, temp2¹⁾ +10/+30, nominal 264 g, initial zero²⁾ ≤214 g, pan Ø 90 mm
- Col 3: BC-EB/BC-AB (again per OCR), Class II, Max 0.1-100 g, e 1-2 mg, d 0.1-2 mg, n ≤ 100000, temp1 +10/+30, temp2¹⁾ +10/+30, nominal 264 g, initial zero²⁾ ≤263 g, pan Ø 90 mm

Hmm wait, for the third column: Max 0.1-100 g with e = 1-2 mg: n = Max/e = 100g/1mg = 100,000. OK that's consistent with n ≤ 100000. And Max = 0.1 g... with e = 1 mg? That gives n=100. Hmm, but ranges are just ranges of possible configurations.

Actually maybe the third column is a different type like "BC-EB BC-AB" — could be OCR of "BC-EB BC-AB"... I'll just take it as is. Since model IDs must be unique within model_family.models, I'll differentiate: "BC-EB/BC-AB (class Ⅰ)" and "BC-EB/BC-AB (class Ⅱ)".

Table 2:
- Col 1: BC-EC/BC-AC, Class I, Max 500-1500 g, e 10-20 mg, d 1-20 mg, n ≤ 150000, temp1 +17/+27, temp2¹⁾ +10/+30, nominal 1800 g, initial zero²⁾ ≤1300 g, pan Ø 120 mm
- Col 2: BC-ED/BC-AD, Class II, Max 1-650 g, e 0.01-0.1 g, d 0.001-0.1 g, n ≤ 65000, temp1 +10/+30, temp2¹⁾ +10/+30, nominal 780 g, initial zero²⁾ ≤779 g, pan Ø 120 mm

Table 3:
- Col 1: BC-EE/BC-AE, Class II, Max 500-6200 g, e 0.1-1 g, d 0.01-1 g, n ≤ 62000, temp +10/+30 (no temp range 2 row — colspan 2 for temp range 1, and no temp range 2 row at all), nominal 7440 g, initial zero²⁾ 6940 g (no ≤ sign!), pan 180mm x 180mm
- Col 2: BC-EF/BC-AF, Class II, same, Max 500-6200 g, e 0.1-1 g, d 0.01-1 g, n ≤ 62000, nominal 7440 g, initial zero 6940 g, pan Ø 180 mm

Table 4:
- Col 1: BC-EG/BC-AG, Class II, Max 5000-12200 g, e 1 g, d 0.1-1 g, n ≤ 12200, temp +10/+30, nominal 14640 g, initial zero²⁾ ≤ 9640 g, pan 180 mm x 180 mm
- Col 2: BC-EH/BC-AH, Class II, same, pan Ø 180 mm

So overall the models are: BC-EA/BC-AA, BC-EB/BC-AB (I), BC-EB/BC-AB (II), BC-EC/BC-AC, BC-ED/BC-AD, BC-EE/BC-AE, BC-EF/BC-AF, BC-EG/BC-AG, BC-EH/BC-AH.

Hmm, but the module says "BC-EA to BC-EH, BC-AA to BC-AH". Each table column pairs an E-variant with an A-variant. So maybe each column actually represents TWO models (BC-EA and BC-AA) with identical characteristics. I could model them as 16 models, or as 9 paired columns. The pairing "BC-EA BC-AA" suggests both models share the characteristics in that column. To be faithful, I'll create model entries per pairing, e.g., model_id "BC-EA / BC-AA". Or list them individually: model_id "BC-EA", "BC-AA" with same values.

I think the cleanest: models[] entries with model_id being the pair "BC-EA/BC-AA" and a label noting both. Alternatively, individual models each duplicating values. The schema says model_family models: {model_id, label, attributes{}}. I'll use paired IDs like "BC-EA / BC-AA" since characteristics are shared, and in model_level values reference those same IDs.

Hmm, but "type_designations[]": all type/model identifiers mentioned: BC-EA, BC-AA, BC-EB, BC-AB, BC-EC, BC-AC, BC-ED, BC-AD, BC-EE, BC-AE, BC-EF, BC-AF, BC-EG, BC-AG, BC-EH, BC-AH. Plus the line names "BC-E", "BC-A"? The Type is "Precision and analysis balances BC-E and BC-A Line"; Module: "BC-EA to BC-EH, BC-AA to BC-AH".

For the third column of table 1 with duplicate type names — OCR issue. I'll denote the model as "BC-EB / BC-AB (class Ⅱ)" to keep uniqueness.

Characteristics handling:

Since Max, e, d, n vary per model, they belong to model_level matrix. The ranges like "50 g - 320 g" become {min: 50, max: 320} with unit "g". e "1 mg - 2 mg" → {min: 1, max: 2} mg. d "0.1 mg - 2 mg" → {min: 0.1, max: 2} mg. n "≤ 320 000" → {min: null, max: 320000} (dimensionless).

Temperature range 1: model-level: +17/+27 for BC-EA/AA, BC-EB/AB(I), BC-EC/AC; +10/+30 for others.
Temperature range 2¹⁾: +10/+30 for all models that have it (BC-EA through BC-EH except BC-EE..BC-EH which don't have temp range 2 rows). Note footnote 1: "Only for weighing instruments with incorporated span adjustment device being automatically released."

Tare-balancing range: "until 100% of Max" → type_level: tare_balancing_range: value "100% of Max"? Per rule about "150% of Emax" → value 150 unit "%" plus reference. Hmm. "until 100% of Max" — I could do value: 100, unit_symbol: "%", and a separate reference. Simpler: value: {min: null, max: 100}, unit "%", reference Max. Let me use: {"attribute": "tare_balancing_range", "value": {"min": null, "max": 100}, "unit_symbol": "%"} plus maybe "tare_balancing_range_reference": "Max". Or keep as string "up to 100% of Max". The rule 2 says formulas/symbols keep as string. "100% of Max" is a value referencing Max. I'll do value 100, unit "%", and add attribute "tare_balancing_range_reference": {"value": "Max"}. Hmm, that might be over-engineering. Actually the schema example for safe_overload: value 150 unit "%" plus separate characteristic safe_overload_reference: {value: "Emax"}. So follow that pattern: tare_balancing_range: {value: {min: null, max: 100}, unit_symbol: "%"} and tare_balancing_range_reference: {value: "Max"}. Hmm, "until 100% of Max" means up to 100% of Max. OK.

Nominal capacity of the load receptor: per model: 384, 264, 264, 1800, 780, 7440, 7440, 14640, 14640 g.

Initial zero setting + dead load²⁾: ≤234, ≤214, ≤263, ≤1300, ≤779, 6940 (no ≤), 6940, ≤9640, ≤9640 g. Footnote 2.

Maximum weighing pan size: Ø 90 mm (string "Ø 90" with unit mm? The Ø is a diameter symbol). I'll record value: 90, unit: "mm", and maybe a separate note for diameter. Alternatively value string "Ø 90", unit mm. Rule: pull unit out; "Ø" is not a unit. For "180 mm x 180 mm" → value {min: 180, max: 180}? It's a rectangular pan 180×180 mm. Could record as string "180 x 180" with unit mm. I think value as string is more faithful: "180 x 180". Hmm, but rule 2 says numbers not strings when numeric. A 180×180 mm pan is a 2-D dimension. I could record two characteristics: pan_width and pan_depth? That complicates. Options: value: "180 x 180", unit_symbol: "mm". Or model_level with per-model values; for round pans value: 90 with note diameter. To keep structured: I'll use value {min: 180, max: 180}? That's a range interpretation — wrong semantics. I'll use string "180 x 180" for rectangular and "Ø 90" for round, unit mm. Actually maybe better: "maximum_weighing_pan_size" with value "Ø 90" / "180 x 180" and unit_symbol "mm". The Ø isn't a footnote or unit; keeping it in the value string preserves meaning. I think that's acceptable as strings for non-scalar dims.

Accuracy class is per model: type_level? It varies per model, so model_level attribute "accuracy_class" with values "Ⅰ" / "Ⅱ". Note roman numerals Ⅰ Ⅱ (unicode). I'll use "I" and "II" (ASCII) to be safe. The certificate uses (Ⅰ) and (Ⅱ). I'll write "Ⅰ" and "Ⅱ"? JSON with unicode fine. But ASCII "I"/"II" safer for downstream. The cert's accuracy_classes at certificate level: ["Ⅰ","Ⅱ"] — I'll use ["I", "II"].

Now structure:

certificate:
- number: "R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.01 Rev. 1." — hmm, maybe cleaner "R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.01" with revision in revision_history. The number as printed: "R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.01 Rev. 1." The annex says "R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.01 Revision 1". I'll put number: "R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.01" and note revision via revision_history (revision "1"). The schema has revision_history separately; number probably without "Rev. 1". I'll include number "R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.01" — trimming trailing period. Hmm "Rev. 1." trailing period is sentence punctuation. I'll use "R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.01".
- scheme: "A"
- project_number: not present. The test report numbers 6030-1189 relate. There's also "CH-W1-19027-01" doc file. No explicit project number field — omit.
- page_total: 4 (pages 1/4..4/4). Include 4.
- member_state: "Switzerland"
- date_issued: "2020-09-21" (21 September 2020)
- oiml_issuer_id: "CH1" ("The OIML Issuing Authority CH1")

- name: "Federal Institute of Metrology METAS" (Conformity Evaluation Body METAS-Cert)
- address_lines: ["Lindenweg 50", "3003 Bern-Wabern", "Switzerland"] — the markdown gives "Lindenweg 50, 3003 Bern-Wabern, Switzerland". I'll split into lines: ["Lindenweg 50", "3003 Bern-Wabern", "Switzerland"].

manufacturers: same as applicant ("The manufacturer of the certified pattern is the applicant.")

certified_type:
- category: hmm. It's a balance/weighing instrument. R76-1 is non-automatic weighing instruments. Category list example: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", ... I'll use "Non-automatic weighing instrument" or "Balance". The doc calls them "Precision and analysis balances". Category: "Balance" seems apt; but recommendation R76 = NAWI. I'll use "Non-automatic weighing instrument (precision and analysis balances)". Hmm, simpler: "Balance". Let me use "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — hmm. The schema says category examples include various; balance isn't listed but the list is open. I'll put "Balance (non-automatic weighing instrument)". Actually simplest faithful: "Precision and analysis balances"? That's the type description. I'll set category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" and description with the balance names. Hmm, but "Don't fabricate" — the instrument category is implied by R76. I'll go with "Balance" — safe, directly from text ("Precision and analysis balances"). Let me choose "Non-automatic weighing instrument" as category since R 76-1 covers NAWIs; the type_designations and description carry the balance specifics. Hmm... I think "Balance" is more directly grounded. I'll use category: "Balance", description: "Precision and analysis balances BC-E and BC-A Line, models BC-EA to BC-EH and BC-AA to BC-AH." Wait — but let me reconsider: the field example list includes "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter" — instrument categories. "Balance" fits that pattern. Good.
- type_designations: ["BC-E", "BC-A", "BC-EA", "BC-AA", "BC-EB", "BC-AB", "BC-EC", "BC-AC", "BC-ED", "BC-AD", "BC-EE", "BC-AE", "BC-EF", "BC-AF", "BC-EG", "BC-AG", "BC-EH", "BC-AH"]. Include all mentioned. The "Module" field: "BC-EA to BC-EH, BC-AA to BC-AH".
- module_designation: For R76 the "module" concept... here "Module" field in METAS cert = the module range "BC-EA to BC-EH, BC-AA to BC-AH". The schema's module_designation is for load cell modules like "Analog load cell" — but here the cert uses "Module" to list model variants. I'll put module_designation: "BC-EA to BC-EH, BC-AA to BC-AH".
- description: "Precision and analysis balances BC-E and BC-A Line" — the type field. Maybe description combines.

- models: list each. I'll create entries:
  1. {model_id: "BC-EA / BC-AA", label: "Class I, Max 50 g – 320 g"} — hmm labels maybe unnecessary. I'll give model_id as the pair and label describing.
  
Actually, should models be individual (16) or paired (9)? The table columns pair them because characteristics are identical. Using paired IDs keeps matrix compact and faithful. But then model_level values reference pair IDs like "BC-EA / BC-AA". I think that's fine and clear. Alternatively define 16 models and duplicate values — verbose but each model individually addressable. Given downstream use, individual models might be more useful. Hmm. The certificate's own presentation pairs them. The instruction example for R60 created model IDs from Emax values. For R137, model_id = size. Here, the natural model identity includes the pair. I'll use pairs: "BC-EA / BC-AA" etc., and for the duplicate BC-EB/BC-AB, "BC-EB / BC-AB (class Ⅰ)" and "BC-EB / BC-AB (class Ⅱ)". Use ASCII "I"/"II" maybe: "BC-EB / BC-AB (class I)" and "BC-EB / BC-AB (class II)".

Wait, is it plausible that the third column is actually a different model pair, e.g., "BC-EB BC-AB" is OCR duplicate of what should be something else? The Module says BC-EA to BC-EH — 8 models. Table pairs: EA, EB, EB(?), EC, ED, EE, EF, EG, EH = 9 columns. With EB duplicated, we have 8 distinct pairs. So indeed BC-EB/BC-AB appears in two columns — class I and class II versions. That's plausible: same hardware family certified in both classes with different Max/e. Actually Sartorius Entris II: models BCE224... hmm. Whatever — I'll keep as is with class disambiguation.

- tare_balancing_range: {value: {min: null, max: 100}, unit_symbol: "%"} plus tare_balancing_range_reference: {value: "Max"}. Hmm, is tare range same for all models? Yes — all tables say "until 100% of Max". So type_level. I'll include:

Units differ per model! mg vs g. Hmm. The structured value has unit per attribute entry... but values[] entries have {model, value, footnote_markers} — no per-value unit. The schema shows "column_units" in matrix_tables for per-column units. For model_level, unit_symbol is at attribute level. Problem: e and d have different units across models. Options: (a) convert all to mg: e: 1-2 mg, 1-2, 1-2, 10-20, 10-100, 100-1000, 100-1000, 1000, 1000 mg. (b) two entries per attribute with unit groups: "verification_scale_interval_e" with unit "mg" for first four models, and another with unit "g"? That's hacky. (c) keep value strings like "0.01 g – 0.1 g" with unit per attribute... no.

Cleanest: convert to a common unit, mg, for e and d. e (mg): EA/AA {1,2}, EB/AB I {1,2}, EB/AB II {1,2}, EC/AC {10,20}, ED/AD {10,100}, EE/AE {100,1000}, EF/AF {100,1000}, EG/AG 1000, EH/AH 1000.

Alternatively include unit_symbol per value via extra key... The schema value objects in model_level have {model, value, footnote_markers} — I could add unit per value? Not per schema. Converting to mg is cleaner and lossless. But is conversion "fabrication"? It's unit conversion — acceptable I think. Hmm, but safer might be to keep original units and split into two attribute entries: "verification_scale_interval_e" (unit mg) covering models with mg, and... no, that duplicates attribute semantics.

Actually, let me reconsider: I could put unit_symbol: "g" and give all in g: e: 0.001-0.002 g etc. mg is more readable. I'll use mg with a note? There's no notes field. Fine — convert to mg.

Hmm, wait — actually maybe better to preserve the certificate's units exactly since the schema's model_level has a single unit_symbol per attribute but I can create separate attribute entries when units differ.
